title: native runtime CUDA profile and cross-device recovery

claim.to_prove: On a real CUDA-capable host, the native sparse runtime can gain measured performance while preserving checkpoint, structure, lineage, budget, provider artifact, and numerical-tolerance contracts.
claim.must_not_claim: CPU measurements are not CUDA support or GPU speedup; no fused/custom kernel is justified before a real profile identifies its bottleneck.

trace.determinism: Record seed, device, dtype, runtime, workload digest, and tolerance; do not compare unbound timing numbers across hosts.
trace.current_evidence: CPU profile and checkpoint continuation are valid baseline evidence only.

checkpoint.cross_device: CPU -> CUDA -> CPU must restore and continue within the declared numerical tolerance; exact identity is required for non-numerical state.
checkpoint.failure: An unavailable or failed device must return hardware-blocked/failed without mutating the CPU baseline.

red_proof: CUDA absent but gate says passed
custom kernel hides a profiled hotspot
OOM is silently retried as success
evidence.holdout: Use a fixed workload revision plus a second seed and a shape/dtype combination not used for kernel selection.
evidence.lesion: Disable the proposed optimization or one transfer/cache path; report the measured delta and preserve correctness.
evidence.cross_seed: Performance acceptance requires multiple seeds or repeated runs with confidence intervals; correctness requires independent checkpoint continuations.

failure_isolation.hardware_missing: Remain hardware-blocked; do not install a fake CUDA fixture as performance proof.
failure_isolation.numerical_drift: Reject optimized path and keep the profiled baseline.
failure_isolation.oom_or_timeout: Abort the experiment, preserve parent checkpoint, and record structured failure.

rollback.path: disable optimized dispatch and restore the last CPU/native runtime checkpoint
rollback.atomicity: Kernel selection, runtime manifest, and checkpoint revision publish together or not at all
rollback.recovery: Re-run the unchanged baseline workload before proposing another optimization.

boundary: No CUDA claim or speedup number may be derived from this CPU-only host.
No custom kernel may encode fixed fan-in or fixed topology as Taiji identity.
CUDA is an execution backend; it does not own Taiji cognition or learning semantics.
